reconcile.connective: Defenders treat the thirty-talent gap as a copyist's slip, Keil & Delitzsch tracing it to one Hebrew numeral letter being mistaken for another.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells catalogues the passages side by side and presses that the same voyage cannot have yielded both 420 and 450 talents — one of the two figures is simply wrong.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (contra: "How many talents of gold did Hiram send Solomon?")
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013); skepticsannotatedbible.com, hiram.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: The difference between 420 and 450 may be accounted for from the substitution of the numeral letter נ (50) for כ (20).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly addresses the 420-vs-450 gap and offers the scribal numeral-letter confusion as the harmonizing explanation; the single strongest, cleanest reconcile sentence on the row (block-anchored).

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on 1 Kings 9:26
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats the 420-vs-450 figure directly, listing the harmonizing options — thirty talents spent on the voyage or wages, Grotius's ore-vs-purified-gold reading, or separate voyages — and concludes "either way removes the difficulty."

link.note: No on-topic page found on an allowlisted domain for the 420-vs-450 figure; link omitted rather than guessed.
